Open-Source AI Engineering Curriculum Expands with Multi-Language Support and Practical Labs

An open-source educational project titled "AI Engineering from Scratch," maintained by Rohit Ghumare and community contributors, provides structured learning resources focusing on model internals, retrieval pipelines, and agent runtimes. Distributed under the MIT license, the repository features 542 lessons organized across 20 phases, with implementations available in multiple programming languages including Python, TypeScript, Rust, and Julia.

Curriculum Structure and Features

The repository covers a range of technical topics, progressing from fundamental mathematical concepts through neural network layers to advanced agent architectures and production workflows.

  • Core Curriculum: Twenty phases exploring foundational mathematics, model components, and system evaluations.
  • Specialized Tracks: Focused pathways covering the Model Context Protocol (MCP), Agent Skills, and Agent-Assisted Engineering.
  • Certification Prep: Independent study programs designed to support preparation for public exam objectives, such as Claude certification tracks and the Model Context Protocol Associate exam.

Interactive Labs and Reusable Artifacts

Each lesson follows a structured format emphasizing practical implementation. Learners build algorithms from scratch before utilizing production libraries. The repository includes runnable labs, interactive figures, diagnostics, quizzes, and reusable code artifacts that can be installed locally or integrated into daily developer workflows.

Verification and Access

Users can inspect the curriculum directly through the official website or the GitHub repository (`rohitg00/ai-engineering-from-scratch`). The project supports local execution using standard tools like Python 3.10+ and Node.js for specific tasks, alongside automated scripts to verify code syntax and run invariant checks. Detailed documentation and installation instructions are available in the public repository.
